definition_zh: 限制；局限于；禁闭
definition_en: to keep something within limits, or to keep a person in one place
core_image: 一圈低矮的篱笆，把羊群圈在草地内
scene: 医生嘱咐他把活动范围限制在家里。The doctor told him to confine his activity to the house.
sceneCN: 这里 confine 指「限制」（第 1 个义项：把范围限定在某个界限内）；句意是医生嘱咐他把活动范围限制在家里。

senses.title: Keep within limits
senses.definition: to keep an activity or subject inside a fixed limit
senses.definitionCN: 把活动或话题限定在固定的范围之内
senses.example: Please confine your remarks to the topic.
senses.exampleCN: 请把发言限制在这个话题之内。
senses.why: A boundary makes a discussion sharp instead of endless.
senses.whyCN: 有了边界，讨论才会集中，而不是漫无边际。

senses.title: Keep in one place
senses.definition: to keep a person or animal in a closed space
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物关在封闭的空间里
senses.example: The prisoner was confined to a small cell.
senses.exampleCN: 那名囚犯被关在一间小牢房里。
senses.why: Walls do to a body what rules do to a topic.
senses.whyCN: 墙对身体的限制，正如规则对话题的限制。

intro.en: Confine comes from Latin confinare, to share a border, from com-, together, and finis, a boundary.
intro.cn: confine 来自拉丁语 confinare，意为共有一条边界，由 com-（一起）与 finis（边界）构成。

items.en: Finis meant the end or the border of a place.
items.cn: finis 意为一个地方的终端或边界。

items.en: Confinare meant to place something inside a border.
items.cn: confinare 意为把某物放进边界之内。

items.en: Old French confiner meant to keep within a district.
items.cn: 古法语 confiner 意为把某物限制在一个区域内。

items.en: English confine first meant to border on a place.
items.cn: 英语 confine 最初指与某地接壤。

items.en: It now means to limit a subject or shut a person in.
items.cn: 如今它指限制一个话题，或把人关起来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confine, and the meaning group names other ways of setting limits.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confine 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他设定限界的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a low fence around sheep, then move to a short speech and to a narrow cell.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围住羊群的低篱笆开始，再走到短短的发言与狭小的牢房。

normal.en: A confined space feels small because the walls are doing their job.

branches.en: Both senses draw a line that cannot be crossed.

branches.en: A confined answer is often a clearer one.

branches.en: A confined space is small by design, not by accident.

definition_zh: 确认；证实；批准；使坚定
definition_en: to show that something is true, or to make a plan or arrangement certain
core_image: 服务员在本子上把订位时间又圈了一遍
scene: 酒店前台打来电话，再次确认明天的房间。Please confirm your booking by email.
sceneCN: 这里 confirm 指「确认」（第 1 个义项：把已有安排再核实一遍）；句意是请通过邮件确认你的预订。

senses.title: Make an arrangement certain
senses.definition: to state that an arrangement is still true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项安排仍然有效或将会发生
senses.example: Please confirm your booking by email.
senses.exampleCN: 请通过邮件确认你的预订。
senses.why: A plan spoken once can drift, and a second word pins it down.
senses.whyCN: 计划只说一次会飘走，再说一次才能把它钉住。

senses.title: Show that a fact is true
senses.definition: to provide evidence that a report or belief is correct
senses.definitionCN: 提供证据说明某个说法或想法是正确的
senses.example: The test confirmed his guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测试证实了他的猜测。
senses.why: Evidence turns a private guess into something others must accept.
senses.whyCN: 证据把私下的猜测变成别人必须接受的事实。

senses.title: Give official approval
senses.definition: to formally approve an appointment or decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准一项任命或决定
senses.example: The council confirmed the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准了新计划。
senses.why: A decision becomes final only when the proper body says yes.
senses.whyCN: 决定只有经有权机构点头，才算最终定下。

items.en: Firmare meant to make something firm or secure.

items.en: Confirmare added com- to strengthen something completely.

items.en: Old French confermer carried the sense of making an agreement secure.

normal.en: A test confirms a guess the way a key confirms a lock.

branches.en: Proof and approval both end a period of uncertainty.

definition_zh: 确认；证实；确认函；坚振礼
definition_en: the act of confirming something, a message or document that confirms it, or the religious rite that strengthens a person's faith
core_image: 落下印章：把还悬着的事按实、定住
scene: 这组词中，After the guest paid the deposit, the hotel sent a confirmation with the room number and check-in time.
sceneCN: 这里 confirmation 是「预订确认」（第 5 个义项：预订确认函）；句意：客人付了定金后，酒店寄来一份写有房号和入住时间的确认函。图中可辨识物件：预订确认邮件、房号、入住时间、付款收据。

pos.zh: 确认函；确认书；（宗教）坚振礼

collocations.zh: 确认偏误（只找支持自己看法的证据）

senses.title: The act of making something certain
senses.titleCN: 确认行为：把不确定变为确定
senses.definition: the act of showing that something is true, valid, or definitely arranged
senses.definitionCN: 证明某事为真、有效或已经确定的行为
senses.example: The lab asked for confirmation of the results before publication.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室要求在发表前先确认这些结果。
senses.why: confirmare is con- 'thoroughly' plus firmare 'to make firm', from firmus 'firm'. The suffix -ation turns that act into a noun, so confirmation is literally 'the making-firm' — the act itself, before it names any document.
senses.whyCN: confirmare 是 con-“彻底”加 firmare“使坚固”，后者出自 firmus“坚固”。后缀 -ation 把这个动作变成名词，因此 confirmation 字面上就是“使坚固这件事”——先指行为本身，还不指任何文件。

senses.title: A message that confirms
senses.definition: an email, letter, or message that states that an arrangement is definite
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项安排已经确定的邮件、信件或消息
senses.example: She received a confirmation within minutes of booking the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她订完机票几分钟后就收到了确认消息。
senses.why: Action nouns in -ation can name the result as well as the act. Once the making-firm is finished, the thing that carries it — the message — is also called a confirmation, because the paper or email now holds the firmness.
senses.whyCN: -ation 类动作名词既能指行为，也能指结果。一旦“使坚固”完成，承载它的东西——那条消息——也被叫作 confirmation，因为纸张或邮件此时替人保存了这份确定。

senses.title: Confirmation bias: the mind proving itself right
senses.titleCN: 确认偏误：只找支持自己的证据
senses.definition: the tendency to notice and trust information that supports what one already believes
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于注意并相信支持自己既有看法的信息
senses.example: Confirmation bias led the team to notice only the data that supported its plan.
senses.exampleCN: 确认偏误让团队只注意到支持自己计划的数据。
senses.why: This 20c psychological term keeps the 'making firm' image but turns it inward: the mind seeks evidence that firms up a belief it already holds. Here confirmation is not a message from outside but an act of self-reinforcement.
senses.whyCN: 这个 20 世纪的心理学词保留了“使坚固”的意象，却把它转向内部：心智去寻找能让既有信念更坚固的证据。这里的 confirmation 不是外来消息，而是一种自我加固的动作。

senses.title: A hearing that confirms an appointment
senses.definition: a formal hearing in which a committee examines a nominee before approving the appointment
senses.definitionCN: 委员会在批准任命前审查被提名者的正式听证会
senses.example: The senate held a confirmation hearing for the new judge.
senses.exampleCN: 参议院为这位新法官举行了确认听证会。
senses.why: In this political branch, 'make firm' is applied to a person's official standing: the nominee is not securely in office until the appointment is confirmed. The hearing is the procedure that produces that firmness.
senses.whyCN: 在这一政治分支里，“使坚固”作用于一个人的官方地位：任命未经确认，被提名者就还没有稳稳地进入职位。听证会就是产生这份确定性的程序。

senses.title: A booking confirmed in writing
senses.definition: a document or message that proves a reservation, ticket, or booking is final
senses.definitionCN: 证明预订、机票或订房已经最终生效的文件或消息
senses.example: Keep your confirmation in case the front desk cannot find the reservation.
senses.exampleCN: 把确认函留着，以防前台找不到这条预订记录。
senses.why: The commercial sense is 20c: a reservation stays provisional until the hotel makes it firm in writing. The document that performs this act then takes the name of the act itself, a common pattern in travel and booking language.
senses.whyCN: 商业义是 20 世纪的产物：预订在酒店以书面方式将其“定实”之前都只是暂定的。完成这一动作的文件于是直接继承了动作的名字，这在旅游和预订用语中很常见。

senses.title: The sacrament that strengthens faith
senses.titleCN: 坚振礼：坚固信仰的圣礼
senses.definition: a religious rite in which a baptized person affirms their faith and is said to receive strength from the Holy Spirit
senses.definitionCN: 受洗者确认自己的信仰、并被认为从圣灵获得力量的宗教仪式
senses.example: In some churches, young people receive confirmation at about thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些教会里，年轻人十三岁左右接受坚振礼。
senses.why: The religious sense is the oldest in English, recorded in the 13c. Latin firmare also meant 'strengthen', so confirmation became the sacrament that strengthens baptismal faith. The original metaphor of making firm is here applied to a person's belief.
senses.whyCN: 宗教义是英语里最古老的一支，13 世纪已有记录。拉丁语 firmare 同时有“使强壮”之意，因此 confirmation 成了坚固受洗信仰的圣礼。原本“使坚固”的比喻在这里落到了人的信念上。

senses.title: A receipt that confirms payment
senses.titleCN: 收据确认：证明款项已付
senses.definition: a receipt or stamp that officially acknowledges that money has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认款项已付的收据或印章
senses.example: The cashier stamped the receipt as confirmation of payment.
senses.exampleCN: 收银员在收据上盖章，作为付款确认。
senses.why: Here -ation again names the concrete evidence of an act: the stamped receipt is the making-firm of a payment, proof that the transaction will not be reopened. The thing that fixes the record borrows the name of the fixing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ation 又指动作的具体证据：盖了章的收据就是付款的“使坚固”，是这笔交易不会再有争议的证明。固定记录的那件东西，借用了“固定”这个动作的名字。

senses.title: A test that confirms an earlier result
senses.definition: a second test carried out to check a provisional result from an earlier test
senses.definitionCN: 为检查先前初步结果而进行的第二次测试
senses.example: A confirmatory test was run after the first screen gave a faint line.
senses.exampleCN: 初筛出现浅线后，又做了一次验证性测试。
senses.why: Confirmatory is confirm plus -atory 'serving to'. A confirmatory test is a second act of making firm, ordered precisely because the first result was not yet firm. Confirmation here names that second stage rather than a document.
senses.whyCN: confirmatory 是 confirm 加 -atory“用于……的”。验证性测试就是第二次“使坚固”，之所以要做，正是因为第一次结果还不够牢靠。这里的 confirmation 指那个第二阶段，而不是文件。

senses.title: An official statement by an authority
senses.titleCN: 官方确认：权威机构的正式声明
senses.definition: a public statement from an official body that settles a report or rumour
senses.definitionCN: 官方机构就某报道或传言作出的、使其尘埃落定的公开声明
senses.example: The ministry issued an official confirmation of the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部发布了关于这次疫情的官方确认。
senses.why: An official confirmation is the state's version of making firm: an authority's published word turns a rumour into a settled fact. The noun gains weight from the institution, which is why 'official' so often precedes it.
senses.whyCN: 官方 confirmation 是国家版本的“使坚固”：权威机构公开表态，传言才变成确定的事实。这个名词的分量来自机构本身，所以 official 常与它连用。

intro.en: Confirmation is the Latin verb confirmare fitted with the action-noun suffix -ation. The religious branch is the earliest recorded in English; the commercial booking sense is a 20c addition. Exact first dates differ between dictionaries, so the centuries below are approximate.
intro.cn: confirmation 是拉丁动词 confirmare 加上动作名词后缀 -ation 构成的。英语中最早记录的是宗教分支；商业预订义则是 20 世纪的增补。各家词典标注的首见年代并不一致，下面几个世纪均为大致估计。

items.en: The base is firmus 'firm, solid', which produced the verb firmare 'to make firm, strengthen'. The prefix con- 'together, thoroughly' intensifies it into confirmare 'to strengthen, establish, ratify'.
items.cn: 底层是 firmus“坚固的、结实的”，由此产生动词 firmare“使坚固、使强壮”。前缀 con-“一起、彻底”加强它，构成 confirmare“加固、确立、批准”。

items.en: Latin turned the verb into the action noun confirmatio (stem confirmation-), built with -atio. English borrowed this pattern as -ation, which names both the act of making firm and, later, the thing that records it.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 -atio 把动词变成动作名词 confirmatio（词干 confirmation-）。英语以 -ation 接受这一构词模式，它既指“使坚固”的行为，后来又指记录这一行为的东西。

items.en: The religious sense is recorded in English in the 13c: confirmation as the sacrament that strengthens a baptized person's faith. This is the earliest English branch, and it preserves the 'strengthen' side of firmare.
items.cn: 宗教义在 13 世纪已见于英语：confirmation 指坚固受洗者信仰的圣礼。这是英语中最早的分支，它保留了 firmare 的“使强壮”一面。

items.en: From the 14c onward, confirm and confirmation are used for the formal ratification of charters, treaties and appointments. Here 'make firm' becomes a legal act: an authority puts its weight behind an arrangement. Precise dating is approximate.
items.cn: 从 14 世纪起，confirm 与 confirmation 用于对特许状、条约和任命的正式批准。这里“使坚固”变成法律行为：权威为某项安排背书。确切年代只能大致估计。

items.en: The everyday sense 'proof that something is true' broadens in the 17c–19c: confirmation of a report, a theory or a result. The noun now covers evidence as well as the act of producing it.
items.cn: “某事物为真的证据”这一日常义在 17 至 19 世纪扩大：对报道、理论或结果的 confirmation。此时名词既指产生证据的行为，也指证据本身。

items.en: The 20c adds booking and email confirmations, along with confirmation bias and confirmation hearings. The old image survives: each branch fixes something that was still provisional. The exact coinage date of the booking sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 20 世纪又添出预订确认、邮件确认，以及 confirmation bias 和 confirmation hearing。旧意象仍在：每个分支都在把原本暂定的事情定下来。预订义的确切产生年代存疑。

note.en: The first group collects words that look or sound close to confirmation; the second collects words with a nearby meaning. Form is checked before meaning, because the -ation ending is a common trap.
note.cn: 第一组是与 confirmation 形音相近的词；第二组是意思相近的词。先看词形，因为 -ation 词尾是常见的混淆点。

entries.definition: to make something certain, valid, or officially approved. It is the verb behind confirmation, not another noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事确定、有效或获正式批准。它是 confirmation 背后的动词，而不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: the arrangement or shape of something, especially a molecule. It also ends in -ation but comes from conformare (con- + forma 'shape'), so it means arrangement, not making firm.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的排列或形状，尤指分子构象。它同样以 -ation 结尾，却来自 conformare（con- + forma“形状”），因此意思是“排列成形”，不是“使坚固”。

entries.definition: a person who is about to receive the religious rite of confirmation. The -and suffix marks someone who is to undergo the action.
entries.definitionCN: 即将接受坚振礼的人。后缀 -and 标记将要经历该动作的人。

entries.definition: the process of checking whether something is true or accurate. It stresses the investigation, while confirmation stresses the settled result.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事物是否真实或准确的过程。它强调调查过程，而 confirmation 强调已经落定的结果。

entries.definition: the act of proving or officially accepting that something is valid. It often implies a formal test or approval, closer to a technical confirmation.
entries.definitionCN: 证明或正式认可某事物有效的行为。它常含正式检验或批准的意味，更接近技术性的 confirmation。

entries.definition: formal approval of an agreement or appointment, making it legally binding. It is narrower and more legal than confirmation.
entries.definitionCN: 对协议或任命的正式批准，使其具有法律约束力。它比 confirmation 更窄、更偏法律。

entries.definition: evidence that supports a statement or theory. It adds separate proof from another source, while confirmation can be a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 支持某项陈述或理论的证据。它强调来自另一来源的独立佐证，而 confirmation 可以只是一次确认动作。

entries.definition: a positive statement that something is true or that one supports it. It is spoken and personal, whereas confirmation may be documentary or official.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定某事为真或表示支持的正面陈述。它偏口头和个人，而 confirmation 可以是书面或官方的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces con- and firm, the real suffix -ation, and the real derivative family of confirm.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分 con- 与 firm、真实的后缀 -ation，以及 confirm 真实的派生词族。

normal.en: The core is firm: confirmare = con- 'thoroughly' + firmare 'make firm'. A confirmation is the act that leaves a fact firm rather than wobbling.
normal.cn: 核心是 firm：confirmare = con-“彻底”+ firmare“使坚固”。confirmation 就是让事实不再摇晃、稳稳立住的那个动作。

normal.en: confirm and affirm share the same firmare base; ad- 'to' gives affirm, while con- 'thoroughly' gives confirm. Both make a statement firm, from different directions.
normal.cn: confirm 与 affirm 共用 firmare 词基：ad-“向”构成 affirm，con-“彻底”构成 confirm。两者都让陈述变坚固，只是方向不同。

normal.en: -ation does double duty: it names the act (the confirmation of a theory) and the artefact (the hotel confirmation). The context decides which one you have.
normal.cn: -ation 有双重职责：既指行为（对理论的 confirmation），也指产物（酒店的确认函）。语境决定你遇到的是哪一个。

normal.en: Confirmation bias is the same 'make firm' turned inward: the mind keeps selecting evidence that firms up what it already believes.
normal.cn: confirmation bias 是同一个“使坚固”转向内部：心智不断挑选能让既有信念更坚固的证据。

normal.en: The religious sense rests on the other meaning of firmare, 'to strengthen': confirmation strengthens baptismal faith, which is why the rite kept the old word.
normal.cn: 宗教义依靠 firmare 的另一层意思“使强壮”：confirmation 坚固受洗的信仰，所以这个仪式沿用了这个老词。

abstract.en: Picture soft wax under a seal: before the press it can still be changed, after it cannot. Confirmation is the press, the seal, and the hardened wax all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象印章下的软蜡：按压之前还能改，按压之后就不能了。confirmation 同时是按压、印章和变硬的蜡。

abstract.en: The same press appears as a lab result, an email, a Senate hearing, a receipt and a sacrament; the material changes, the fixing does not.
abstract.cn: 同一次按压会以实验结果、邮件、参议院听证、收据和圣礼出现；材料变了，固定这件事没变。

abstract.en: A belief that only seeks its own evidence is a seal pressed by the mind on its own wax: the impression is real, but the wax was chosen by the presser.
abstract.cn: 只寻找自身证据的信念，是心智在自己的蜡上按下印章：印痕是真的，但蜡是按压者自己选的。

examples.en: Please send a confirmation once the payment has cleared.
examples.cn: 款项到账后请发一份确认。

examples.en: The senate held a confirmation hearing for the new judge.
examples.cn: 参议院为这位新法官举行了确认听证会。

examples.en: In some churches, young people receive confirmation at about thirteen.
examples.cn: 在一些教会里，年轻人十三岁左右接受坚振礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「肯费美申」：肯（con）费（fir）美（ma）申（tion）——肯花力气，把申请审实定案 → confirmation 确认；确认函

root: confirm（con- 加强 + firmare 使坚固，源自 firmus 坚固）+ -ation 名词后缀；核心是“把不牢靠的事变坚固、定下来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of confirmation, all one gesture: something provisional is pressed into a firm state, whether the thing fixed is a fact, a booking, a belief, an appointment, a payment or a person's faith.
sensesIntro.cn: confirmation 的九个义项都是同一个动作：把暂定之物压成确定状态——被固定住的可以是事实、预订、信念、任命、付款或一个人的信仰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed onto soft wax, turning something provisional into something fixed.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章压在软蜡上，把暂定之物变成固定之物。

branches.en: ACT AND MESSAGE: first the act of making firm, then the message or document that carries the firmness.
branches.cn: 行为与消息：先有“使坚固”的动作，再有承载这份确定性的消息或文件。

branches.en: MIND AND TEST: the same press turned inward, where a belief confirms itself or a second test confirms a first result.
branches.cn: 心智与检验：同一次按压转向内部——信念自我加固，或第二次测试确认第一次的结果。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: a nominee or a report becomes firm only when an institution formally confirms it.
branches.cn: 权威：被提名者或报道只有在机构正式确认后才变得确定。

branches.en: COMMERCE: bookings and payments are fixed in writing, and the written proof inherits the name of the act.
branches.cn: 商业：预订与付款靠书面固定下来，书面凭证继承了动作的名字。

branches.en: SACRAMENT: firmare as 'strengthen' becomes the rite that strengthens a person's faith.
branches.cn: 圣礼：firmare 的“使强壮”化为坚固个人信仰的仪式。

intro.en: Confirmation is one of the most transparent -ation nouns: confirm is a living English verb, and -ation is a living suffix that turns it into an act or its result. The word is not a single opaque borrowing.
intro.cn: confirmation 是最透明的 -ation 名词之一：confirm 是活的英语动词，-ation 是活的后缀，把它变成行为或行为的结果。它不是一整块不可拆的借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin confirmare 'to strengthen, establish' is built from con- and firmare, and its action noun confirmatio supplies the -ation pattern. The same firmus base gives firm, firmness and affirm, so the family is wider than the confirm- words alone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 confirmare“加固、确立”由 con- 与 firmare 构成，其动作名词 confirmatio 提供了 -ation 模式。同一个 firmus 词基还给出 firm、firmness、affirm，因此这个词族比 confirm- 系列更宽。

items.meaning: to make something certain or officially valid
items.meaningCN: 确认；证实；批准（con- 表“彻底”，firm 表“使坚固”）
items.example: The airline confirmed the new departure time by email.
items.exampleCN: 航空公司通过邮件确认了新的起飞时间。

items.meaning: the act of confirming, or the message that confirms
items.meaningCN: 确认；确认函（-ation 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The confirmation arrived before we reached the airport.
items.exampleCN: 我们到机场之前确认函就到了。

items.meaningCN: 已确认的；根深蒂固的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The confirmed cases rose sharply that week.
items.exampleCN: 那一周确诊病例数急剧上升。

items.meaning: the act of confirming, or something that confirms
items.meaningCN: 确认中的；起确认作用的（-ing 构成现在分词）
items.example: The confirming letter settled the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 那封确认信解决了争议。

items.meaning: serving to confirm an earlier result
items.meaningCN: 验证性的；用于确认的（-atory 表“用于……”）
items.example: A confirmatory scan followed the first X-ray.
items.exampleCN: 第一次 X 光之后又做了一次验证性扫描。

items.meaning: able to be confirmed or verified
items.meaningCN: 可确认的；可证实的（-able 表“能够被……”）
items.example: The claim is confirmable with two independent sources.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法可以用两个独立来源加以确认。

items.meaningCN: 未经确认的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Reports of the closure remain unconfirmed.
items.exampleCN: 关于关闭的报道仍未得到确认。

items.meaning: to confirm again, especially a booking
items.example: Guests must reconfirm their seats two hours before departure.
items.exampleCN: 旅客必须在起飞前两小时再次确认座位。

items.meaning: to show that something is not true
items.meaningCN: 否定；证伪（dis- 表反转或否定）
items.example: The new evidence disconfirmed the earlier theory.
items.exampleCN: 新证据否定了先前的理论。

definition_zh: 冲突；矛盾；争执；抵触
definition_en: a serious disagreement between people or groups, or a state of being opposed
core_image: 两股人马在窄路上迎面顶住，谁也不肯退
scene: 两个部门为了预算在会上争得面红耳赤。The conflict between the two teams slowed the project.
sceneCN: 这里 conflict 指「冲突」（第 1 个义项：双方之间的严重对立）；句意是两个团队之间的冲突拖慢了项目。

senses.title: A serious disagreement
senses.definition: a long or serious disagreement between people, groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团体或国家之间长时间或严重的分歧
senses.example: The conflict lasted for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突持续了许多年。
senses.why: Two sides want opposite things, and neither will step back.
senses.whyCN: 双方想要相反的东西，谁都不肯退让。

senses.title: A clash between ideas or rules
senses.definition: a situation where two ideas, rules or duties cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 两种想法、规则或职责无法同时成立的情形
senses.example: There is a conflict between the two rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条规则之间存在矛盾。
senses.why: A rule and a rule can fight just as two people can.
senses.whyCN: 规则与规则也会打架，就像两个人一样。

senses.title: To be opposed to
senses.definition: to be different from something in a way that cannot be reconciled
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物不同且无法调和
senses.example: His words conflict with his actions.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言语与行动相抵触。
senses.why: What is said and what is done can point in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 说的和做的，可能指向相反的方向。

intro.en: Conflict comes from Latin conflictus, a striking together, from confligere, to strike against.
intro.cn: conflict 来自拉丁语 conflictus，意为相互撞击，源自 confligere（彼此打击）。

items.en: Fligere meant to strike or knock something down.
items.cn: fligere 意为打击或击倒某物。

items.en: Confligere meant to strike two forces against each other.
items.cn: confligere 意为让两股力量彼此撞击。

items.en: Conflictus named the clash itself.
items.cn: conflictus 指撞击这件事本身。

items.en: French conflit carried the sense into disputes between people.
items.cn: 法语 conflit 把这个意思带入人与人之间的争端。

items.en: English conflict now covers war, argument and contradiction alike.
items.cn: 英语 conflict 如今同时覆盖战争、争吵与自相矛盾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that end like conflict, and the meaning group names other kinds of clash.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conflict 词尾相近的词，近义组列出其他表示冲突的说法。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in court
to make something narrow or tight
to cause pain or trouble to someone
a serious argument about something
a short and sharp disagreement or fight
a hard fight to get or change something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two crowds meeting in a narrow lane, then move to two rules and to words that do not match actions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两群人在窄巷相遇开始，再走到两条规则与言行不一的场面。

normal.en: Con- is together and flict is strike, so conflict is two forces striking together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，flict 是打击，所以 conflict 就是两股力量撞在一起。

normal.en: A conflict of interest means two duties want the same seat.
normal.cn: 利益冲突，就是两种职责抢同一把椅子。

normal.en: Armed conflict is the same clash with weapons added.
normal.cn: 武装冲突，就是同一个撞击加上了武器。

normal.en: Two rules in conflict cannot both be followed at once.
normal.cn: 两条相互抵触的规则，不可能同时遵守。

normal.en: When words conflict with actions, believe the actions.
normal.cn: 当言语与行动冲突时，相信行动。

abstract.en: Picture two waves breaking against each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两道浪迎面相撞。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows painted on one road.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路上画着两支方向相反的箭头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pushing one door from both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手从两边推同一扇门。

examples.en: The two countries ended a long conflict.
examples.cn: 两国结束了一场长期冲突。

examples.en: There is a conflict between profit and safety.
examples.cn: 利润与安全之间存在矛盾。

examples.en: That rule conflicts with the older one.
examples.cn: 那条规则与旧规则相抵触。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conflict 记成 con（一起）加 flict（打击）：两边一起动手互打，就是冲突；两条规则撞在一起，就是矛盾。

root: 源自拉丁语 conflictus（con 一起 + fligere 打击），本义是相互撞击，后引申为冲突、矛盾与抵触。

sensesIntro.en: From two forces striking, to two rules contradicting, and finally to words that do not match deeds.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两股力量相撞，到两条规则相悖，最后到言行对不上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two crowds meet in a narrow lane and neither will turn back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两群人在窄巷相遇，谁都不肯回头。

branches.en: The social sense is a clash between people with opposite aims.
branches.cn: 社会义项是目标相反的人之间的对撞。

branches.en: The logical sense is a clash between statements that cannot both hold.
branches.cn: 逻辑义项是两句不能同时成立的话之间的对撞。

branches.en: The verb sense describes the state of being opposed.
branches.cn: 动词义项描述彼此对立的状态。

branches.en: People and rules can both gridlock at a narrow point.
branches.cn: 人与规则都可能在狭窄处僵住。

branches.en: Contradiction and opposition are the same shape in different places.
branches.cn: 矛盾与对立，是同一种形状出现在不同地方。

intro.en: Conflict is built on Latin com-, together, plus fligere, to strike.
intro.cn: conflict 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 fligere（打击）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin strike base flict- also appears in inflict and afflict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的打击词基 flict- 也出现在 inflict 与 afflict 中。

items.example: The region has seen many conflicts.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区经历过许多冲突。

items.example: Her duties conflicted with her wishes.
items.exampleCN: 她的职责与愿望发生了冲突。
我们收到了相互矛盾的报道。

items.meaning: not able to be true together
items.exampleCN: 这两个答案是彼此冲突的。
他对离开感到内心矛盾。
他们研究了一段充满冲突的关系。
暴风雨造成了严重破坏。

definition_zh: 遵守；符合；顺从（规则、习俗）；与……一致
definition_en: to act according to a rule, standard, or expectation, or to match a pattern, shape, or model
core_image: 一块湿泥被按进同一个模子里，边角与模子严丝合缝
scene: 这组词中，In his first week at the bank, he shaved his beard and bought three grey suits to conform.
sceneCN: 这里 conform 是「从众、照着大家的样子做」（第 3 个义项：迎合群体的做法与品味）；句意：进银行的第一周，他就刮掉胡子、买了三套灰西装，以便和大家一样。场景要点：一间办公室、一片灰色西装、一个新来的人把自己调进同一个模子。

derivatives.zh: 顺从者；墨守成规的人／顺从的
不遵奉常规的人；不从众的

senses.title: Be obedient to a higher authority
senses.definition: to submit one's behaviour to the command of God, a superior, or an accepted authority
senses.definitionCN: 使自己的行为服从上帝、上级或公认权威的命令
senses.example: The monks conformed to the rule of silence from the first bell.
senses.exampleCN: 从第一声钟响起，修士们就遵守静默的规定。
senses.why: Latin conformare meant 'to fashion, shape'. To obey was originally to let a higher authority press you into its mould, so obedience and shaping were one act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 conformare 本义是“塑造、做成形状”。服从最初就是让更高的权威把你按进它的模子，因此服从与塑形曾是同一个动作。

senses.title: Act in accordance with an example
senses.definition: to behave in the way that a model, example, or established practice prescribes
senses.definitionCN: 按照范本、例证或既定做法所规定的方式行事
senses.example: The new branch conformed to the parent company's accounting format.
senses.exampleCN: 新分公司照搬了母公司的会计格式。
senses.why: Late 14th-century English added 'bring into harmony; act in accordance with an example'. The mould is now an example rather than a person, but the copy is still exact.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪晚期英语又添上“使之和谐、依照范例行事”一义。模子此时从一个人变成一份范例，但复制仍然要求严丝合缝。

senses.title: Social conformity: fitting in with the group
senses.definition: to adopt the dress, habits, or opinions of a group in order to belong to it
senses.definitionCN: 为了融入群体而采用该群体的穿着、习惯或观点
senses.example: Teenagers often conform to the group's taste in music before they ever question it.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年往往在质疑之前，就已经顺从了群体的音乐品味。
senses.why: If the mould belongs to a group, fitting it means giving up whatever shape was yours. The word keeps the pressure of the mould and loses none of its discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 如果模子属于一个群体，嵌进去就意味着放弃你原本的形状。这个词保留了模子的压力，也保留了其中全部的不适。

senses.title: Religious conformity to an established church
senses.definition: in English history, to accept the doctrines and forms of worship of the established church
senses.definitionCN: 在英国历史上，指接受国教的教义与礼拜形式
senses.example: In the 1630s, clergymen who refused to conform to the prayer book lost their posts.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪 30 年代，拒绝遵奉祈祷书的教士被免职。
senses.why: From the 1610s the word named acceptance of the Church of England's forms. A form of worship is literally a shape, so the original metaphor and the religious usage meet again.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 10 年代起，这个词指接受英格兰教会的礼拜形式。礼拜的 form 字面就是“形状”，因此原初的比喻与宗教用法在这里重新重合。

senses.title: Match a shape or specification
senses.definition: of an object, to have exactly the shape, size, or specification required
senses.definitionCN: 指物体具有完全符合要求的形状、尺寸或规格
senses.example: The replacement part conforms to the original thread size.
senses.exampleCN: 替换零件的尺寸与原装螺纹规格完全吻合。
senses.why: This is the mould image at its most literal: the metal part must take precisely the shape left by the specification, with no room for individual variation.
senses.whyCN: 这是模子意象最字面的一次：金属件必须精确地嵌进规格留下的形状，不留任何个体差异的余地。

senses.title: Comply with a law or regulation
senses.definition: to meet the requirements of a law, code, or official rule
senses.definitionCN: 满足法律、规范或官方规则的要求
senses.example: All shipments must conform with the new labelling rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有货物都必须遵守新的标签规定。
senses.why: A regulation is a mould drawn by a legislature: a product or procedure conforms when it can pass through that outline without forcing it open.
senses.whyCN: 法规是立法者画出的模子：产品或流程能顺着这个轮廓通过而不把它撑开，就是 conform。

senses.title: Fit a model or prediction
senses.definition: of data or behaviour, to agree with what a theory, model, or prediction says should happen
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或行为与理论、模型或预测所说的应当发生的情况相符合
senses.example: The results conformed to the model's prediction within two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 结果与模型的预测误差在百分之二以内。
senses.why: Here the mould is a theory. Observing that the data take its shape is what lets a scientist say the model holds; the word marks agreement between pattern and instance.
senses.whyCN: 这里的模子是理论。观察到数据长成它的形状，科学家才能说这个模型成立；这个词标记的是模式与个例之间的一致。

senses.title: Adapt to local custom
senses.definition: to adjust one's behaviour to the unwritten expectations of a place or culture
senses.definitionCN: 使自己的行为适应某一地方或文化中不成文的期待
senses.example: She conformed to local dining customs without abandoning her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她遵从了当地的餐桌习俗，但也没有丢掉自己的。
senses.why: The shaping is now voluntary and temporary: a traveller bends to a local outline for a while, then keeps the original shape underneath.
senses.whyCN: 这里的塑形是自愿而暂时的：旅人暂时弯进当地的轮廓，但底下仍保留原来的形状。

senses.title: Bring one thing into harmony with another
senses.titleCN: 使一物与另一物相协调
senses.definition: to make something consistent with or fitted to something else, often in a formal or technical context
senses.definitionCN: 使某物与另一物一致或相嵌合，常用于正式或技术语境
senses.example: The architect conformed the new wing to the slope of the old roof.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师让新侧翼与旧屋顶的坡度相协调。
senses.why: The transitive use goes back to 'bring into harmony' in the late 14th century: instead of being pressed into a mould, the maker presses one thing into the outline of another.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法可追溯到 14 世纪晚期的“使之和谐”：不是自己被按进模子，而是制造者把一件东西按进另一件东西的轮廓里。

intro.en: Conform comes from Latin conformare 'to fashion, shape', built on forma 'form, shape'. Its whole history is the history of being fitted to a mould.
intro.cn: conform 来自拉丁语 conformare“塑造、做成形状”，建立在 forma“形状、形式”之上。它的全部历史，就是“被嵌进一个模子”的历史。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'be obedient (to God), comply'. The earliest sense is religious and moral, not technical.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 14 世纪中叶，意为“（对上帝）服从、遵从”。最早的义项是宗教与道德性的，而不是技术性的。

items.en: A second branch appears: 'bring into harmony; act in accordance with an example'. The transitive 'make consistent' and the intransitive 'follow a model' grow side by side.
items.cn: 第二条分支出现：“使之和谐；依照范例行事”。及物的“使一致”与不及物的“照范本做”并排生长。

items.en: English borrowed the verb through Old French conformer, which had already narrowed the Latin word toward obedience and agreement.
items.cn: 英语经由古法语 conformer 借入这个动词，法语已把拉丁词义收窄到“服从”和“一致”。

items.en: Conformare joins com- 'together' (here intensive, 'completely') and formare 'to form, shape', from forma 'form, shape, mould'.
items.cn: conformare 由 com-“一起”（此处为加强义“完全”）和 formare“使成形、塑造”组成，后者来自 forma“形状、形式、模子”。

items.en: In the 1610s the word was applied to accepting the forms of the Church of England; conformist, the label for one who does so, is dated to the 1630s.
items.cn: 17 世纪 10 年代，这个词被用来指接受英格兰教会的礼拜形式；指称这样做的人的 conformist 可追溯到 17 世纪 30 年代。

items.en: Conform must not be confused with confirm. Conform rests on forma 'shape'; confirm rests on Latin firmus 'firm, strong', from confirmare 'to strengthen, establish'. The two words are not related, despite their near-identical spelling.
items.cn: conform 不可与 confirm 混淆。conform 的根基是 forma“形状”；confirm 的根基是拉丁语 firmus“坚固、牢固”，来自 confirmare“使坚固、确立”。尽管拼写几乎一样，二者并非同源词。

note.en: The first group is the dangerous one: three words that look almost like conform but come from a different root or a different suffix. The second group collects verbs of following a rule.
note.cn: 第一组最危险：三个词看起来几乎和 conform 一样，却来自不同词根或不同后缀。第二组收集表示“按规则行事”的动词。

entries.definition: to prove or establish that something is true; to ratify. It looks like conform and sounds close to it, but its root is Latin firmus 'firm, strong', from confirmare 'strengthen'. Forma 'shape' plays no part in it.
entries.definitionCN: 证实或确认某事为真；批准。它看起来、听起来都近似 conform，但词根是拉丁语 firmus“坚固、牢固”，来自 confirmare“使坚固”。forma“形状”与它毫无关系。

entries.definition: a person who behaves according to accepted standards, often used with disapproval. The -ist suffix turns the verb into the person who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 按公认标准行事的人，常带贬义。后缀 -ist 把动词变成“做这件事的人”。

entries.definition: a person who refuses to follow established customs or doctrines; also a member of a Protestant church outside the Church of England. The non- prefix reverses the fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝遵循既定习俗或教义的人；也指英格兰教会之外的新教教徒。前缀 non- 把“嵌合”反转过来。

entries.definition: the fact of meeting a standard or specification, common in industry and testing. It is close to conformity but more technical and countable in quality-control contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 符合标准或规格的事实，常用于工业与检测。它与 conformity 相近，但在质量控制语境中更技术化。

entries.definition: to act in accordance with an order, rule, or request. Comply stresses doing what is required; conform stresses taking the required shape.
entries.definitionCN: 按命令、规则或请求行事。comply 强调做出被要求的行为；conform 强调变成被要求的形状。

entries.definition: to do what a person in authority tells you to do. Obey is personal and direct, while conform can be impersonal, driven only by a norm or a pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 听从有权威者的指令。obey 是人对人的、直接的；conform 可以是非人称的，只由规范或模式驱动。

entries.definition: to change oneself or something else so that it fits a new situation. Adapt stresses change and adjustment; conform stresses matching a fixed outline.
entries.definitionCN: 改变自己或他物以适应新情况。adapt 强调改变与调整；conform 强调与一个固定轮廓相吻合。

entries.definition: to follow a rule, agreement, or belief closely; literally, to stick to a surface. Adhere is about loyalty to a commitment, conform about shape-matching.
entries.definitionCN: 严格遵守规则、协议或信念；字面义为“黏附在表面”。adhere 强调对承诺的忠诚，conform 强调形状上的吻合。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts and real relatives: com- 'together', forma 'shape', and the living pair conformity / conformist. The confirm contrast is spelling only, not etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实的构词成分与真实同族词：com-“一起”、forma“形状”，以及常用成对的 conformity／conformist。与 confirm 的区别只在拼写，不在词源。

normal.en: con- means 'together' and forma means 'shape'. To conform is to take the same shape as everyone else in the group.
normal.cn: con- 是“一起”，forma 是“形状”。conform 就是长成和群体中其他人一样的形状。

normal.en: The suffix -form appears in many real words: form, format, formula, uniform, transform. All of them carry the idea of shape, which is the true core here.
normal.cn: 后缀 -form 出现在许多真实单词里：form、format、formula、uniform、transform。它们都带着“形状”这个观念，而形状正是这个词真正的核心。

normal.en: Conform is not confirm. Conform = take the shape (forma); confirm = make firm (firmus). Remember 'forma' when you see the o in conform.
normal.cn: conform 不是 confirm。conform = 取形状（forma）；confirm = 使坚固（firmus）。看到 conform 里的 o，就想起 forma。

normal.en: A conformist takes the group's shape; a nonconformist refuses it. The non- prefix does not change the root, only the decision.
normal.cn: conformist 接受群体的形状；nonconformist 拒绝它。non- 前缀改变的不是词根，只是那个决定。

normal.en: In manufacturing, conformance is a measurable thing: the part either fits the specification or it does not. That is the mould image made testable.
normal.cn: 在制造业，conformance 是可测量的事情：零件要么符合规格，要么不符合。这就是模子意象被做成了可检验的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a single iron mould and a queue of soft clay blocks. Each block loses its own edges as it enters, and comes out identical to the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一个铁模子和一队软泥块。每一块在进入时失去自己的边角，出来时和其余的一模一样。

abstract.en: The mould can be a god, a school, a company, a law, a theory, or a local custom. The pressure is the same; only the authority holding the mould changes.
abstract.cn: 模子可以是神、学校、公司、法律、理论，也可以是当地习俗。压力是一样的，变的只是握着模子的那个权威。

abstract.en: Conformity is comfortable and costly at the same time: you gain belonging, and you give up the edges that made you recognisable.
abstract.cn: 从众同时是舒适和昂贵的：你得到了归属，也交出了那些让人认得出你的边角。

examples.en: The packaging must conform to the safety standard before it can be sold.
examples.cn: 包装必须符合安全标准才能销售。

examples.en: He refused to conform to the office's unspoken rule about working late.
examples.cn: 他拒绝遵从办公室那条关于加班的潜规则。

examples.en: The village church was built to conform with the older chapel beside it.
examples.cn: 这座村庄教堂的建造方式与旁边那座更古老的礼拜堂相协调。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯仿”——肯照着别人的样子仿，大家最后都长成一个模子 → conform 遵从、符合

root: 源自拉丁语 conformare“塑造、做成形状”，由 com-“一起”+ forma“形状”构成，核心是“把自己嵌进同一个模子”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of conform, all grown from one action: something takes the shape of a mould. The mould may be God, a rule, a group, a church, a specification, a law, a theory, a local custom, or another object.
sensesIntro.cn: conform 的九个义项都从同一个动作长出来：某物嵌进一个模子的形状。模子可以是神、规则、群体、教会、规格、法律、理论、当地习俗，也可以是另一件东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft material pressed into a fixed mould and coming out in its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：软材料被按进固定模子，出来时是模子的形状。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: God, a superior, or an established church holds the mould, and obedience is the act of entering it.
branches.cn: 权威：上帝、上级或国教握着模子，服从就是走进去的动作。

branches.en: SOCIETY: an example or a group supplies the outline, and the individual gives up personal edges to fit it.
branches.cn: 社会：范例或群体提供轮廓，个人交出个人的边角以嵌进去。

branches.en: SPECIFICATION: a part, a product, or a procedure must pass through the outline drawn by a standard or a law.
branches.cn: 规格：零件、产品或流程必须顺着标准或法律画出的轮廓通过。

branches.en: MODEL: data takes the shape a theory predicts, and that agreement is what confirms the model.
branches.cn: 模型：数据长成理论预测的形状，这种一致正是模型得到确认的依据。

branches.en: ADJUSTMENT: a traveller bends to local custom, or a maker presses one thing into the outline of another.
branches.cn: 调整：旅人暂时弯进当地习俗，或制造者把一件东西按进另一件东西的轮廓。

intro.en: Conform is one of the few words in this batch whose Latin parts are still fully transparent in English: con- plus forma, and the suffix -form survives in dozens of everyday words.
intro.cn: conform 是本批少数几个拉丁成分在英语里仍然完全透明的词：con- 加 forma，而且 -form 这个成分在几十个日常单词里存活下来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on forma 'shape': formare 'to shape', conformare 'to shape together', and conformis 'similar in shape'. English also borrowed forma through French as form, and built conformable and conformance on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 forma“形状”上：formare“使成形”、conformare“一起塑形”、conformis“形状相似的”。英语还经法语借入 forma 作 form，并在同一词干上造出 conformable 与 conformance。

items.meaning: the state of matching a rule or of behaving like others
items.meaningCN: 符合；遵从；一致性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The audit checks conformity with the accounting standard.
items.exampleCN: 审计检查是否符合会计准则。

items.meaning: the fact of meeting a specification
items.meaningCN: （对规格的）符合；一致性（-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: The factory issued a certificate of conformance.
items.exampleCN: 工厂出具了一份符合性证书。

items.meaning: a person who follows accepted standards
items.meaningCN: 顺从者；墨守成规的人（-ist 构成人称名词）
items.example: He was too much of a conformist to challenge the manager.
items.exampleCN: 他太顺从了，不敢质疑经理。

items.meaning: a person who refuses established customs or doctrines
items.meaningCN: 不遵奉常规的人；不从众者（non- 表示否定）
items.example: As a nonconformist, she wore red to the all-black party.
items.exampleCN: 她一向不从众，在所有人都穿黑衣的聚会上穿了红色。

items.example: The report noted repeated nonconformity with the safety code.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出多次不符合安全规范的情况。

items.meaning: able to be made to fit or to agree
items.meaningCN: 可使之符合的；顺从的（-able 表示“能够被”）
items.example: The old rules are conformable to the new treaty.
items.exampleCN: 旧规则可以调整到与新条约一致。

items.meaning: in a way that matches a rule or standard
items.meaningCN: 以符合的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The site was built conformably with the zoning plan.
items.exampleCN: 该场地是按分区规划建造的。

items.meaning: meeting a standard; also the act of matching
items.meaningCN: 符合的；遵从的（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: Only conforming products may carry the safety mark.
items.exampleCN: 只有符合标准的产品才能加贴安全标志。

latinEntries.meaning: to fashion, form, shape; to make consistent
to strengthen, establish, confirm; the source of English confirm, NOT of conform
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使坚固、确立、确认；这是英语 confirm 的来源，与 conform 无关

definition_zh: 遵从；一致性；符合；从众
definition_en: behaviour that matches the accepted standards of a group, or the state of agreeing with a rule, standard, or shape
core_image: 同一个模子里倒出的两块砖：边角贴合，严丝合缝
scene: 这组词中，On their first day, the new technicians learned that conformity to the lab's safety routine was expected at every step.
sceneCN: 这里 conformity 是「遵守规则」（第 2 个义项：按规则行事）；句意：上班第一天，新技师就被告知，每一步都必须遵守实验室的安全流程。图中可辨识物件：安全流程看板、护目镜、手套、实验台。

derivatives.zh: 符合性（多用于技术标准）

senses.title: Behaviour shaped to accepted norms
senses.titleCN: 遵从规范：行为照着群体的样子
senses.definition: the state or habit of behaving according to the accepted standards of a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 按照群体或社会认可的标准行事的状态或习惯
senses.example: Small towns often expect a degree of conformity in dress and manners.
senses.exampleCN: 小城镇往往要求人们在穿着和举止上有所遵从。
senses.why: conformare is con- 'together' plus forma 'shape, mold': to give the same shape. The suffix -ity names a state, so conformity is the condition of having taken the group's mold. The first sense is that shape in daily behaviour.
senses.whyCN: conformare 是 con-“共同”加 forma“形状、模子”：使具有同一形状。后缀 -ity 表示状态，因此 conformity 就是“已经取了群体那个模子”的状态。第一个义项就是日常行为上的这种同形。

senses.title: Obeying rules and procedures
senses.definition: the act of following the rules, routines or procedures set by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 遵守权威所定规则、惯例或程序的行为
senses.example: Conformity to safety rules is checked before the plant opens.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂开工前会检查是否遵守了安全规则。
senses.why: A rule works as an abstract forma: it tells behaviour what shape to take. Conformity here is not resemblance to other people but resemblance to the written procedure, so the same 'same shape' idea is applied to a text.
senses.whyCN: 规则就是一个抽象的 forma：它规定行为该取什么形状。这里的 conformity 不是与别人相像，而是与书面规程相像，于是同一个“同形”观念落到了文字上。

senses.title: Social conformity under group pressure
senses.titleCN: 社会从众：在群体压力下随大流
senses.definition: the tendency to change one's behaviour or opinion to match the majority of a group
senses.definitionCN: 改变自己的行为或观点以与群体多数保持一致的倾向
senses.example: The experiment showed that conformity rises when the group is unanimous.
senses.exampleCN: 实验表明，当群体意见一致时，从众程度会上升。
senses.why: This branch is 20c social psychology. The majority supplies the mold and the person takes its shape, often without a conscious decision. The old metaphor of forma is now a mental and social one.
senses.whyCN: 这一支是 20 世纪的社会心理学。多数人提供模子，个人取它的形状，常常并没有做出自觉决定。原先的 forma 比喻这时变成了心理和社会层面的。

senses.title: Agreement with a standard, in conformity with
senses.definition: in the phrase in conformity with, in agreement with a rule, law, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in conformity with，表示与规则、法律或标准相一致
senses.example: The building was designed in conformity with local fire codes.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑是按照当地消防规范设计的。
senses.why: This phrase preserves the original sense most clearly: two things share one forma. A design and a code are said to be in conformity when their shapes coincide, which is why the expression sounds formal and spatial at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语最清楚地保留了本义：两样东西共有一个 forma。设计与规范被称为 in conformity，就是它们的形状重合，所以这个说法既正式又带空间感。

senses.title: Conformity assessment: checking a product against a standard
senses.titleCN: 合格评定：对照标准检查产品
senses.definition: the formal process of testing whether a product or process meets a technical standard
senses.definitionCN: 检验产品或流程是否符合某项技术标准的正式过程
senses.example: The product passed conformity assessment and received the CE mark.
senses.exampleCN: 该产品通过了合格评定，获得了 CE 标志。
senses.why: Industrial standards use conformity as a countable, testable state: the product must take the exact shape described by the specification. Assessment is the act of measuring that match, so the abstract noun becomes a technical procedure.
senses.whyCN: 工业标准把 conformity 当作可检验的状态：产品必须取得规格说明所描述的那个精确形状。评定就是测量这种吻合，于是抽象名词变成了一道技术程序。

senses.title: Matching technical specifications
senses.titleCN: 符合标准：与规格参数吻合
senses.definition: the state of matching the measurements, materials, or performance limits set in a specification
senses.definitionCN: 与规格书规定的尺寸、材料或性能限值相吻合的状态
senses.example: The batch was tested for conformity to the agreed tolerances.
senses.exampleCN: 这批货接受了与约定公差相符性的检测。
senses.why: Here forma has become a number on a drawing. The material is judged by whether it takes that exact shape within tolerance. Conformity is no longer about people at all, only about fit between thing and specification.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 forma 变成了图纸上的一个数字。材料是否合格，要看它能否在公差内取得那个精确形状。conformity 此时与人完全无关，只关乎物与规格之间的贴合。

senses.title: Nonconformity: the state of not matching
senses.definition: the state of not following accepted norms, or of failing to match a required standard
senses.definitionCN: 不遵循公认规范，或未达到规定标准的状态
senses.example: Nonconformity was tolerated in the art school but not in the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术学院容忍不从众，银行则不容忍。
senses.why: non- negates the state while -ity still names it. The contrast is useful: nonconformity can only exist where a norm exists, so the negative form proves that conformity depends on a shared mold.
senses.whyCN: non- 否定这个状态，而 -ity 仍把它命名为状态。这种对照很有用：只有存在规范的地方才有 nonconformity，因此否定形式反而证明 conformity 依赖一个共同模子。

senses.title: The pressure that produces conformity
senses.titleCN: 从众压力：把人压进模子的力
senses.definition: the social force that makes a person adopt the group's behaviour, as in conformity pressure
senses.definitionCN: 使人采纳群体行为的社会压力，如 conformity pressure
senses.example: Teenagers often feel conformity pressure in the first weeks at a new school.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年转学后的头几周常感到从众压力。
senses.why: In conformity pressure the noun is used attributively for the force, not the state. The mold image becomes active: pressure is the hand that presses the person into the group's shape.
senses.whyCN: 在 conformity pressure 中，名词作定语，指那股力而不是状态。模子意象变成主动的：压力就是那只把个人按进群体形状的手。

senses.title: Consistency of behaviour across occasions
senses.titleCN: 行为一致性：前后保持同一形状
senses.definition: the quality of behaving in the same way on different occasions or in different settings
senses.definitionCN: 在不同场合或情境中表现保持一致的性质
senses.example: The study measured conformity by comparing answers given on two visits.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究通过比较两次到访时给出的答案来衡量行为一致性。
senses.why: -ity names a quality, and a quality can be measured over time. If behaviour keeps the same shape from one occasion to the next, it is consistent. This branch drops the group and keeps only the sameness of form.
senses.whyCN: -ity 指一种性质，而性质可以随时间测量。若行为从一个场合到下一个场合保持同一形状，它就是一致的。这一支丢掉了群体，只保留“形状相同”本身。

intro.en: Conformity is the Latin adjective conformis turned into a noun with -itas. Its earliest English sense was 'similarity of form'; only later did it come to mean obedience to norms. Dates for the early senses are approximate.
intro.cn: conformity 是拉丁形容词 conformis 加 -itas 变成的名词。它最早的英语义是“形状相似”，后来才转为“遵从规范”。早期义项的具体年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base is forma 'shape, mold, form'. With con- 'together', Latin formed conformare 'to give the same shape, make alike'. The physical image is two things pressed into one mold.
items.cn: 底层是 forma“形状、模子、外形”。加上 con-“共同”，拉丁语构成 conformare“使有同一形状、使相似”。其物理意象是两样东西被压进同一个模子。

items.en: From conformare came the adjective conformis 'similar in shape', and from it the noun conformitas 'similarity'. The Latin suffix -itas (stem -itatem) becomes English -ity, which names a state or quality.
items.cn: 由 conformare 产生形容词 conformis“形状相似的”，再由它产生名词 conformitas“相似”。拉丁后缀 -itas（词干 -itatem）变成英语 -ity，用来命名状态或性质。

items.en: The English verb conform arrives through Old French conformer in the late 14c. Its first meaning is 'to be of the same form, to correspond', not yet 'to obey'. The exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语动词 conform 经古法语 conformer 在 14 世纪晚期进入。它最初的意思是“具有相同形状、相对应”，还不是“服从”。确切首见年代只能大致估计。

items.en: Conformity is recorded in the 15c first as 'similarity of form, correspondence'. The shift from shape to conduct happens by extension: if a person's behaviour has the same form as a rule, the person is said to conform.
items.cn: conformity 在 15 世纪最早记录为“形状相似、相对应”。从形状到行为的转移靠引申完成：若一个人的行为与规则同形，这个人就被说成 conform。

items.en: The Reformation gives conformity a sharp institutional sense: conformity to the Church of England, and Nonconformity for those who refused it. Here the mold is doctrine and ritual, and 'same shape' becomes obedience to authority.
items.cn: 宗教改革给 conformity 一个鲜明的制度义：对英格兰教会的 conformity，以及拒绝者的 Nonconformity。此时模子是教义与礼仪，“同形”变成了对权威的服从。

items.en: In the 19c–20c the word moves into social science: conformity as the individual taking the group's shape under pressure. Industry adds conformity assessment, and legal prose keeps in conformity with as a fossil of the old 'same form' sense.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，这个词进入社会科学：conformity 指个人在压力下取群体的形状。工业界添出 conformity assessment，法律文本则以 in conformity with 保留旧有“同形”义的化石。

note.en: The first group separates conformity from its own family and from the look-alike conformation; the second groups words that also describe matching or obeying. Form comes first, then meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把 conformity 与它自己的词族以及形近的 conformation 区分开；第二组是同样表示“符合、服从”的词。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: to behave according to a rule or standard, or to have the same form. It is the verb behind conformity, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则或标准行事，或具有相同形状。它是 conformity 背后的动词，不是名词。

entries.definition: the arrangement of parts, especially the shape of a molecule. It shares conformare but keeps the literal 'shape' sense and adds -ation, so it is not the social noun.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的排列，尤指分子构象。它与 conformare 同源，但保留字面的“形状”义并加上 -ation，因此不是那个社会义名词。

entries.definition: a person who accepts and follows established norms. The -ist suffix names the person, while -ity names the state.
entries.definitionCN: 接受并遵循既有规范的人。后缀 -ist 指人，而 -ity 指状态。

entries.definition: the act of obeying a rule, request, or law. It stresses the duty to obey, while conformity can be a social state without a written rule.
entries.definitionCN: 遵守规则、要求或法律的行为。它强调服从的义务，而 conformity 可以是没有成文规则的社会状态。

entries.definition: agreement or consistency with something, used mainly in in accordance with. It is close to in conformity with but more formal and legal.
entries.definitionCN: 与某事物的一致或相符，主要用于 in accordance with。它接近 in conformity with，但更正式、更偏法律。

entries.definition: the practice of keeping a law, rule, or religious custom. It focuses on the act of keeping, not on the state of matching.
entries.definitionCN: 遵守法律、规则或宗教习俗。它侧重“遵守”这个动作，而不是“相合”的状态。

entries.definition: the act of accepting the authority of another. It adds power and surrender, which conformity does not necessarily contain.
entries.definitionCN: 接受他人权威的行为。它带有权力与屈服意味，而 conformity 不一定包含这些。

entries.definition: the quality of following social conventions. It is about taste and custom, while conformity is broader and can concern rules or standards.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循社会习俗的性质。它关乎品味与习俗，而 conformity 范围更广，也可涉及规则或标准。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin forma 'shape', the real suffix -ity, and the real conform / conformist / nonconformity family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语 forma“形状”、真实的后缀 -ity，以及真实的 conform / conformist / nonconformity 词族。

normal.en: forma means 'shape, mold'. conformity is the state (-ity) of having taken that mold, which is why the word works for dress, rules, products and opinions alike.
normal.cn: forma 意为“形状、模子”。conformity 就是取了那个模子的状态（-ity），所以它既能用于穿着，也能用于规则、产品和观点。

normal.en: The family is transparent: conform is the verb, conformist the person, conformity the state, conformation the literal arrangement, nonconformity the refusal.
normal.cn: 词族很清楚：conform 是动词，conformist 是人，conformity 是状态，conformation 是字面的排列，nonconformity 是拒绝。

normal.en: Nonconformity is a historical label as well as a general one: in England it named those who would not take the Church's shape.
normal.cn: Nonconformity 既是普通说法，也是历史标签：在英格兰，它指那些不肯取教会形状的人。

normal.en: in conformity with is the oldest sense still visible: a design and a code share one shape.
normal.cn: in conformity with 是仍然可见的最古老义：一份设计与一份规范共有一个形状。

normal.en: conformity assessment is the industrial version: a product is measured against the shape written in a standard.
normal.cn: conformity assessment 是工业版本：产品对照标准里写下的形状被测量。

abstract.en: Picture two bricks from one mold: their edges fit because they were never separate shapes. Conformity is that fit, whether the mold is a rule, a group, or a standard.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个模子倒出的两块砖：边角贴合，因为它们从来不是两个独立的形状。conformity 就是这种贴合，无论模子是规则、群体还是标准。

abstract.en: A person is softer than brick: the group presses, and the person takes the shape. Conformity pressure is simply the hand doing the pressing.
abstract.cn: 人比砖软：群体一压，人就取了形状。conformity pressure 不过是那只按压的手。

abstract.en: Nonconformity is the piece that refuses the mold; you can see the mold most clearly by the edge that does not fit.
abstract.cn: nonconformity 是拒绝模子的那一块；恰恰通过那条不合的边，模子才最清楚。

examples.en: The school prized conformity over originality.
examples.cn: 这所学校看重遵从，胜过原创。

examples.en: All equipment must be in conformity with the new standard.
examples.cn: 所有设备都必须符合新标准。

examples.en: Nonconformity can be a virtue in a culture that rewards obedience.
examples.cn: 在奖励服从的文化里，不从众也可以是一种美德。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「肯佛米提」：肯（con）佛（for）米（mi）提（ty）——肯照着佛的模子捏米团，形状一致 → conformity 遵从；一致

root: conform（con- 共同 + forma 形状，使同形）+ -ity 名词后缀；核心是“取同一个形状、与规范贴合”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of conformity, all one shape: a person, a product, or a behaviour takes the form of a norm, a group, or a written standard. Nonconformity is the same mold seen from the piece that will not fit.
sensesIntro.cn: conformity 的九个义项都是同一个形状：人、产品或行为取了规范、群体或书面标准的形状。nonconformity 则是从“不肯贴合的那一块”反看同一个模子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two objects pressed from the same mold, so their edges match.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个模子压出的两样东西，边缘彼此吻合。

branches.en: PERSON AND RULES: daily behaviour takes the shape of group norms, and written rules act as an abstract mold.
branches.cn: 人与规则：日常行为取群体规范的形状，书面规则则充当抽象的模子。

branches.en: GROUP PRESSURE: the majority supplies the shape, and pressure is the hand that presses the individual into it.
branches.cn: 群体压力：多数人提供形状，压力则是把个人按进去的那只手。

branches.en: AGREEMENT WITH A STANDARD: two things share one form, whether the standard is a fire code or a tolerance on a drawing.
branches.cn: 与标准一致：两样东西共有一个形状，无论标准是消防规范还是图纸上的公差。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL ASSESSMENT: the match becomes a testable procedure, with the abstract noun turned into a technical step.
branches.cn: 工业评定：这种吻合变成可检验的程序，抽象名词也变成一道技术步骤。

branches.en: NEGATION AND CONSISTENCY: nonconformity shows the mold by refusing it, while consistency keeps the same shape over time.
branches.cn: 否定与一致：nonconformity 以拒绝显示模子的存在，而行为一致性则让同一形状在时间中保持。

intro.en: Conformity is a clean suffix stack: the verb conform, the adjective suffix -ity, and a family that adds -ist, non-, -ance and -able without changing the core forma 'shape'.
intro.cn: conformity 是一组干净的后缀堆叠：动词 conform、名词后缀 -ity，以及一个不断加 -ist、non-、-ance、-able 却不改变 forma“形状”核心的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma 'shape' produces conformare 'to shape together' and conformis 'similar in shape'; conformitas then supplies the -ity noun. English also borrows the same forma in form, formal and formation, so the family is wider than the conformity words alone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma“形状”产生 conformare“使同形”与 conformis“形状相似的”；conformitas 再提供 -ity 名词。英语中 form、formal、formation 也借用同一个 forma，因此词族比 conformity 系列更宽。

items.meaning: to take the same shape, hence to comply
items.meaningCN: 使同形；遵从；符合（con- 表“共同”，form 表“形状”）
items.example: New buildings must conform to the safety code.
items.exampleCN: 新建筑必须符合安全规范。

items.meaning: the state of matching a norm or standard
items.meaningCN: 遵从；一致性；符合（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The survey measured conformity among new employees.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了新员工的从众程度。

items.meaning: a person who follows established norms
items.meaningCN: 遵奉者；循规蹈矩的人（-ist 指人）
items.example: He was too much of a conformist to challenge the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他太循规蹈矩，不会去质疑那条规则。

items.meaning: the state of not matching a norm
items.meaningCN: 不一致；不从众（non- 表否定）
items.example: Nonconformity in the laboratory can be dangerous.
items.exampleCN: 在实验室里不守规矩可能是危险的。

items.meaning: a person who does not follow established norms
items.example: The chapel was built by nonconformists in the 18c.
items.exampleCN: 这座小教堂是 18 世纪不从国教者建造的。

items.meaning: able to be made to fit, or willing to comply
items.meaningCN: 可使之相符的；顺从的（-able 表“能够被……”）
items.example: The material is conformable to the curved surface.

items.meaning: the practice of accepting established norms without question
items.meaningCN: 遵奉主义；因循守旧（-ism 表做法或体系）
items.example: The film satirizes the conformism of suburban life.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片讽刺了郊区生活的因循守旧。

items.meaning: matching a standard, or in the act of complying
items.meaningCN: 符合的；遵从中的（-ing 构成现在分词）
items.example: The conforming units passed the inspection.
items.exampleCN: 符合要求的设备通过了检查。

items.meaning: the state of meeting a technical requirement
items.meaningCN: 符合性（技术标准用语，-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: The software was tested for conformance to the protocol.
items.exampleCN: 该软件接受了协议符合性测试。

latinEntries.meaning: to give the same shape, make alike

definition_zh: 面对；正视；对抗；使面临
definition_en: to face a difficult situation or person directly
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子对视，谁也没有移开目光
scene: 她决定不再回避，直接找对方把问题说清。She decided to confront him about the missing money.
sceneCN: 这里 confront 指「当面质问」（第 2 个义项：直接与当事人对质）；句意是她决定就那笔失踪的钱当面质问他。

senses.title: Face a hard situation
senses.definition: to deal with a difficult problem or fact directly
senses.definitionCN: 直接处理困难的问题或事实
senses.example: We must confront the problem, not hide it.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须正视这个问题，而不是藏起来。
senses.why: A problem faced becomes a task, while a problem avoided becomes a fear.
senses.whyCN: 问题被面对就成了任务，被躲开就成了恐惧。

senses.title: Stand up to someone
senses.definition: to meet a person face to face about a conflict
senses.definitionCN: 为了一件冲突与某人当面对质
senses.example: She confronted him about the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 她就那笔失踪的钱当面质问他。
senses.why: A quiet complaint behind a back is weaker than one clear sentence in front.
senses.whyCN: 背后小声抱怨，比不上当面一句清楚的话。

senses.title: Put face to face with
senses.definition: to make someone have to deal with something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使某人不得不应付困难的事
senses.example: The town is confronted with a water shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇正面临缺水。
senses.why: Some difficulties arrive without invitation and must still be met.
senses.whyCN: 有些困难不请自来，却仍然必须应对。

intro.en: Confront comes from Latin confrontare, to stand face to face, from com-, together, and frons, the forehead or face.
intro.cn: confront 来自拉丁语 confrontare，意为面对面站着，由 com-（一起）与 frons（额头、脸）构成。

items.en: Frons meant the forehead and, by extension, the whole face.
items.cn: frons 意为额头，并引申为整张脸。

items.en: Confrontare meant to bring two faces into the same line of sight.
items.cn: confrontare 意为让两张脸进入同一条视线。

items.en: French confronter used the word for meeting an opponent.
items.cn: 法语 confronter 用这个词表示与对手会面。

items.en: English confront first meant to stand facing someone.
items.cn: 英语 confront 最初指面对面站着。

items.en: It now also means to face a problem or to be faced with one.
items.cn: 如今它也指面对一个问题，或被迫面临某个问题。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confront, and the meaning group names other ways of facing something hard.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confront 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示面对困难的说法。

entries.definition: to admit that you did something wrong
to make someone unable to think clearly
to keep within limits
to deal with something difficult
to question or oppose someone bravely
to make a serious effort to deal with a problem

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two faces across a table, then move to a hard problem and to a town short of water.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从桌子两边对视的脸开始，再走到棘手的问题与缺水的城镇。

normal.en: Con- is together and front is the face, so confront is to put faces together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，front 是脸面，所以 confront 就是把脸对到一处。

normal.en: To confront a problem is to sit down opposite it and look.
normal.cn: 面对问题，就是坐到它对面，然后看着它。

normal.en: A confrontation begins the moment both people stop looking away.
normal.cn: 对峙开始于两个人都不再移开目光的那一刻。

normal.en: Be confronted with bad news and you still choose what to do next.
normal.cn: 被迫面对坏消息时，你仍然可以选择下一步。

normal.en: The front of a building faces the street, and a brave person faces the truth.
normal.cn: 建筑的正面朝向街道，勇敢的人则朝向真相。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs placed exactly opposite each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子正对着摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door you finally push open.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇你终于推开的锁着的门。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of water rising in front of a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵水墙在小镇前升起。

examples.en: The country must confront its water crisis.
examples.cn: 这个国家必须正视自己的水危机。

examples.en: He confronted his friend about the broken promise.
examples.cn: 他就那个没守住的承诺当面质问朋友。

examples.en: We were confronted with a difficult choice.
examples.cn: 我们面临一个艰难的选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confront 记成 con（一起）加 front（正面）：两张脸正面相对，就是面对；面对面提出异议，就是当面质问。

root: 源自拉丁语 confrontare（com 一起 + frons 额头、脸），本义是面对面站着，后引申为面对、对抗与使面临。

sensesIntro.en: From two faces meeting across a table, to meeting a problem, and finally to being pushed into a difficulty.
sensesIntro.cn: 从桌边两张相对的脸，到与问题正面相遇，最后到被推进困境之中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two faces at one table, neither turning aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张桌边的两张脸，谁都不转向别处。

branches.en: Facing a problem is the first act of solving it.
branches.cn: 正视问题，是解决问题的第一个动作。

branches.en: Confronting a person turns a private worry into an open conversation.
branches.cn: 当面质问某人，把私下的担忧变成公开的对话。

branches.en: Being confronted with something leaves no room to look away.
branches.cn: 被迫面临某事时，就再没有转开视线的余地。

branches.en: Both senses pull a hidden matter into the open.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把藏着的事拉到明处。

branches.en: A person can confront another, and a situation can confront us.
branches.cn: 人可以质问另一个人，处境也会反过来逼到我们面前。

intro.en: Confront is built on Latin com-, together, plus frons, the face or forehead.
intro.cn: confront 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 frons（脸、额头）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin face base front- also appears in front, frontal and affront.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的脸面词基 front- 也出现在 front、frontal 与 affront 中。

items.example: Every winter the town confronts deep snow.
items.exampleCN: 每年冬天这个镇都要面对大雪。

definition_zh: 使困惑；使糊涂；混淆；弄错
definition_en: to make someone unable to think clearly, or to mix two things up
core_image: 两条几乎一样的小路在雾里分成岔
scene: 新手看着两张几乎一样的表格，不知该填哪一张。Two similar forms confuse most new applicants.
sceneCN: 这里 confuse 指「使困惑」（第 1 个义项：让人弄不清该怎么办）；句意是两张相似的表格让大多数新申请者都糊涂了。

senses.title: Make someone unsure
senses.definition: to make someone unable to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法理解或无法作出决定
senses.example: The instructions confused everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这些说明让屋里每个人都糊涂了。
senses.why: Too many choices at once leave the mind without a path.
senses.whyCN: 选择一次给得太多，脑子就找不到一条路。

senses.title: Mix two things up
senses.definition: to mistake one person or thing for another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人或一样东西误认成另一个
senses.example: People often confuse the two words.
senses.exampleCN: 人们常常把这两个词混淆。
senses.why: Two things that look alike are stored in the mind almost on the same shelf.

intro.en: Confuse comes from Latin confundere, to pour together, from com-, together, and fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 来自拉丁语 confundere，意为倒在一起，由 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour a liquid out of a container.
items.cn: fundere 意为把液体从容器里倒出来。

items.en: Confundere meant to pour several things into one vessel.
items.cn: confundere 意为把几样东西倒进同一个容器。

items.en: The mixed result was hard to separate again.
items.cn: 混在一起之后，就很难再分开。

items.en: Old French confondre used the image for a confused mind.
items.cn: 古法语 confondre 把这个意象用于混乱的心思。

items.en: English confuse now means to puzzle someone or to mix two things up.
items.cn: 英语 confuse 如今指使人困惑，或把两样东西混淆。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confuse, and the meaning group names other ways of puzzling someone.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confuse 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他让人糊涂的说法。

entries.definition: to admit that you did something wrong
to face a problem or person directly
to say that you will not do something
to make someone think hard without an answer
to confuse someone completely
to give someone a wrong idea

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two paths in fog, then move to two similar forms and to two words on one shelf.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从雾中的两条岔路开始，再走到两张相似的表格与同一层架子上的两个词。

normal.en: Con- is together and fuse is pour, so confuse is to pour everything into one cup.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fuse 是倒，所以 confuse 就是把所有东西倒进一个杯子。

normal.en: A confused mind is a drawer where every sock has the same colour.
normal.cn: 困惑的脑子，就像一个里面每只袜子都同色的抽屉。

normal.en: To confuse two words is to give them one name by mistake.
normal.cn: 混淆两个词，就是误把它们当成同一个名字。

normal.en: Confusing instructions make a simple task look like a maze.
normal.cn: 令人费解的说明，把简单任务变成迷宫。

normal.en: The fog does not move the road; it only hides which road is which.
normal.cn: 雾没有移动道路，只是藏起了哪条是哪条。

abstract.en: Picture two roads splitting inside a grey fog.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路在灰雾中分开。

abstract.en: Picture two liquids meeting in one glass.
abstract.cn: 想象两种液体在同一只杯里相遇。

abstract.en: Picture two labels swapped on two jars.
abstract.cn: 想象两个罐子上的标签被互换。

examples.en: The map confused us more than it helped.
examples.cn: 这张地图没帮上忙，反而让我们更糊涂。

examples.en: Do not confuse being busy with being useful.
examples.cn: 不要把忙碌和有用混为一谈。

examples.en: Her sudden question confused the whole class.
examples.cn: 她突然的提问让全班都愣住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confuse 记成 con（一起）加 fuse（倒）：把好几样东西倒进一个杯子搅在一起，人就分不清了，这就是使困惑与混淆。

root: 源自拉丁语 confundere（com 一起 + fundere 倾倒），本义是倒在一起，后引申为使困惑、混淆与搅乱。

sensesIntro.en: From several liquids poured into one cup, to a mind that cannot tell two things apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从几种液体倒进一只杯子，到一颗分不清两样东西的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads vanish into fog and two labels sit on the wrong jars.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路消失在雾里，两个标签贴错了罐子。

branches.en: Being confused is a state of not knowing which way to go.
branches.cn: 困惑就是不知道往哪边走的状态。

branches.en: Confusing two things means giving one the name of the other.
branches.cn: 混淆两样东西，就是把一个的名字给了另一个。

branches.en: Both senses come from a boundary that has stopped being visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自一条已经看不见的界线。

branches.en: Clear steps are the best cure for a confused mind.
branches.cn: 清楚的步骤是治困惑最好的药。

branches.en: Look-alike words are the easiest pair to confuse.
branches.cn: 长得像的词，是最容易被混淆的一对。

intro.en: Confuse is built on Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pour base fus- also appears in refuse, fusion and suffuse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的倾倒词基 fus- 也出现在 refuse、fusion 与 suffuse 中。

items.example: Do not confuse the two labels.
items.exampleCN: 不要把这两个标签弄混。
这个回答把我弄糊涂了。

items.example: The room was full of confusion.
She looked confused by the question.
items.exampleCN: 她似乎被这个问题问住了。

definition_zh: 困惑；混乱；混淆；骚动
definition_en: a state of not understanding what is happening, or a lack of order
core_image: 雾中的一群人，各朝不同的方向走
scene: 停电之后，大厅里的人不知该往哪个出口走。The sudden darkness caused confusion in the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 confusion 指「混乱」（第 2 个义项：秩序被打乱的状态）；句意是突然的黑暗在大厅里引起了混乱。

senses.title: A puzzled mind
senses.definition: the feeling of not being able to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 无法理解或无法决定的感受
senses.example: His answer left me in complete confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让我完全糊涂了。
senses.why: A mind given too many directions at once stops choosing any.
senses.whyCN: 脑子同时收到太多方向，就一个也不选了。

senses.title: A lack of order
senses.definition: a situation in which things are disordered and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 事物秩序被打乱、难以控制的情形
senses.example: The room was in complete confusion after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬完之后房间里一片混乱。
senses.why: When every object leaves its place, the eye loses its map.
senses.whyCN: 每样东西都离开原位，眼睛就失去了地图。

senses.title: Mixing two things up
senses.definition: the act of treating two different things as the same
senses.definitionCN: 把两样不同的事物当成同一样
senses.example: The confusion of the two names caused real trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名称的混淆带来了真正的麻烦。
senses.why: A name is a handle, and two handles on one door lead to the wrong room.
senses.whyCN: 名字是把手，一扇门上装两个把手就会走错房间。

intro.en: Confusion comes from Latin confusio, a pouring together, from confundere, to pour together.
intro.cn: confusion 来自拉丁语 confusio，意为倒在一起，源自 confundere（混合倾倒）。

items.en: Confusio named the mixed and disordered result.
items.cn: confusio 指混合之后那种杂乱的结果。

items.cn: 英语 confusion 如今覆盖困惑、混乱与认错对象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns with a similar ending, and the meaning group names other states of disorder or doubt.
note.cn: 形近组收的是词尾相近的名词，近义组列出其他表示混乱或疑惑的状态。

something given up in an argument

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a crowd walking in different directions, then move to a moved room and to two names on one door.

normal.en: Confusion is what a room looks like when every chair has forgotten its corner.

normal.en: A crowd in confusion moves fast and arrives nowhere.

normal.en: The confusion of two names is a small mistake with a long shadow.
normal.cn: 两个名字的混淆是小错，却拖着长长的影子。

normal.en: Clear one fact at a time, and confusion begins to thin.
normal.cn: 一次弄清一个事实，混乱就开始变薄。

abstract.en: Picture a fog full of people facing different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾里的人群面朝不同方向。

abstract.en: Picture a desk swept into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被扫成一堆。

abstract.en: Picture two names written on one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门上写着两个名字。

examples.en: There was some confusion about the meeting time.
examples.cn: 关于会议时间有一些混乱。

examples.en: The new signs should clear up the confusion.
examples.cn: 新标志应该能消除这种困惑。

examples.en: In the confusion, nobody noticed the open gate.
examples.cn: 在一片混乱中，没人注意到敞开的大门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confusion 记成 confuse（倒在一起）加 ion：东西全倒在一处，分不清彼此，就是混乱与困惑。

root: 源自拉丁语 confusio（con 一起 + fundere 倾倒），本义是混倒在一起，后引申为困惑、混乱与混淆。

sensesIntro.en: From liquids mixed in one vessel, to a mind without direction, and finally to two things taken for one.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foggy hall where everyone walks a different way.

branches.en: The naming sense is two different things sharing one label.
branches.cn: 命名义项是两样不同的东西共用同一个标签。

branches.en: A disordered room and a disordered mind look surprisingly alike.
branches.cn: 杂乱的房间与杂乱的头脑，看起来出奇地像。

branches.en: Mixing up names is the smallest form of a larger mess.
branches.cn: 弄混名字，是更大混乱中最小的那一种。

intro.en: Confusion is Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour, with the noun ending -ion.

items.meaning: a state of disorder or doubt

items.meaning: the joining of two things into one

definition_zh: adj. 意气相投的，合得来的；宜人的，适宜的
definition_en: pleasant because of a shared nature or a good fit
core_image: 两个人一开口就发现想法彼此合拍
scene: 他发现和她相处格外投缘，一聊就是一下午。He found her congenial company and they talked all afternoon.

senses.title: Suited to a place or task

senses.example: The climate is congenial to health.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的气候有益健康。
senses.why: The fit is between a person and a setting.
senses.whyCN: 这种契合发生在人与环境之间。

intro.en: Congenial joins con-, together, to genius, an inborn nature.
intro.cn: congenial 由 con-（共同）与 genius（天性）构成。

items.en: Genius meant a guardian spirit or inborn nature.

items.en: Genialis meant of birth or festive.

items.en: Congenial described minds of one kind.
items.cn: 十七世纪 congenial 形容同类的心性。

items.en: It spread to pleasant rooms and climates.
items.cn: 十八世纪扩展到宜人的房间与气候。

items.en: It came to mean simply agreeable.

intro.cn: congress 来自拉丁语 congressus，意为走到一起，由 com-（一起）与 gradi（迈步）构成。

items.en: Gradi meant to step or walk forward.
items.cn: gradi 意为迈步或向前行走。

items.en: Congressus named the act of walking together to one place.
items.cn: congressus 指一起走到同一个地方的行为。

items.en: Old French congres used the word for an assembly of people.

items.en: English congress first meant a formal meeting of representatives.

items.en: American usage gave it the sense of a national law-making body.

items.en: It now covers both a single conference and a permanent parliament.
items.cn: 如今它既指一次会议，也指常设的议会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin step base or the ending of congress, and the meaning group names other law-making bodies.

normalIntro.en: Congruity is the fit you feel when nothing is out of place.
normalIntro.cn: congruity 是万物各得其位时感到的协调。

normal.en: Congruere means to come together.
normal.cn: congruere 意为合到一处。

normal.en: Congruity is the state of fitting.
normal.cn: congruity 是相合的状态。

normal.en: Words and deeds can have congruity.
normal.cn: 言行之间可以有一致性。

normal.en: A style can have congruity with its subject.
normal.cn: 风格可以与题材相称。

normal.en: Its adjective is congruent.
normal.cn: 其形容词是 congruent。

abstract.en: Every object in the room in place.
abstract.cn: 屋内每件东西各在其位。

abstract.en: A door that meets its frame.
abstract.cn: 与门框相合的门。

abstract.en: A melody and its bass in step.
abstract.cn: 与低音同步的旋律。

examples.en: The congruity of the parts makes the design calm.
examples.cn: 各部分相称使设计显得安静。

examples.en: We felt a congruity between the music and the film.
examples.cn: 我们感到音乐与影片彼此协调。

examples.en: His dress showed congruity with the occasion.
examples.cn: 他的衣着与场合相称。

dict_mnemonic.text: congru（相合）+ -ity（状态）→ 相合的状态，即一致、适宜。

root: 拉丁 congruere（相合）→ congruitas（相合）→ 英语 congruity

sensesIntro.en: Things agreeing with each other, or suiting the place they are in.
sensesIntro.cn: 彼此相合，或与所处之地相称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything in a room resting in its right place
core.cn: 核心意象：屋内每件东西各在其位

branches.en: A promise matched by action.
branches.cn: 以行动兑现的承诺。

branches.en: Two accounts that agree.
branches.cn: 彼此一致的两份叙述。

branches.en: A dress suited to the hour.
branches.cn: 与场合相称的衣着。

branches.en: A chair shaped to its table.
branches.cn: 与桌子相配的椅子。

branches.en: Rightness of fit, inner or outer.
branches.cn: 内外皆宜的相称。

intro.en: Congruity is the noun of fitting built on congruere.
intro.cn: congruity 是建在 congruere 之上表相合的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin congruere is to agree, congruus is fitting, congruitas is the fit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 congruere 意为相合，congruus 意为相称的，congruitas 指相合。
